solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cloud that's bust in a storm, violently

indicators.note: the words are tossed about as if by a violent storm, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A cloud has burst during a violent storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' rearranges BUSTINASTORM; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a grey, layered rain cloud, one of the standard meteorological cloud types.

clue.text: Hint about his misbehaving like a naughty child

indicators.note: the word for hint goes round the other piece, so it is placed about it

parts.note: to hint is to imply

indicators.note: the letters of the word his behave badly and fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a boy is misbehaving like a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' turns HIS into ISH, and 'about' puts it inside IMPLY, between IMP and LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with mischief, in the manner of a little devil, is exactly how a naughty child behaves.

clue.text: Tolerate Paddington?

definitions.meaning: to tolerate something is to put up with or endure it
Paddington is the famous children's-book animal from Peru, named after a London railway station

explanation.definitionFit: Enduring something means putting up with it, and Paddington is a fictional ursine character.

clue.text: Come to the rescue and put that date in your diary!

definitions.meaning: to rescue a situation at the last moment

definitions.text: put that date in your diary!
definitions.meaning: read literally, an instruction to reserve a particular date in advance

explanation.surface: Someone is told to come and help and to book the date.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means rescuing a situation; read literally it asks you to keep a calendar date free.

clue.text: Track opening old city up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a yawn is a wide opening, as of a mouth or chasm
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A track leads to an excavation opening up an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns YAWN + UR into the answer; Ur of the Chaldees is the crossword's favourite old city.
explanation.definitionFit: An airport's strip for take-off and landing is a kind of track laid on the ground.

clue.text: What will serve as national emblem? It's said the thing here will

definitions.text: What will serve as national emblem?

indicators.note: the words are spoken aloud, so the answer is a sound-alike

parts.note: the thing here is this, so the words mean this will, shortened to this'll

explanation.surface: A question about which symbol will serve the nation, answered that this one will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' says THIS'LL is heard; the prickly plant is Scotland's national emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiky purple-flowered plant is the national flower and emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: At the end of the day is workplace OK?

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed after the day, at its end

parts.note: Sat is the short form of Saturday, a day
taken as written
a factory is a place where people work

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their workplace is fine when the day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of the day' poses as the idiom meaning 'ultimately', but it puts IS FACTORY after SAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acceptable, adequate and passable is all right, which is what OK means.

clue.text: Jazz fan leading dance in China long ago

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
the hay (or hey) is an old English country dance

explanation.surface: A jazz enthusiast leads a dance in old China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' just puts CAT in front of HAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval European name for that East Asian country, used by Marco Polo, is an old poetic term.

clue.text: Conservative politician holding a party

indicators.note: the first pieces hold the next one inside them

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Tory MP is hosting a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction or side within a larger body is a party, as in the opposing sides of a debate.

clue.text: Notice opening made by one holy person who looks for golden age?

parts.note: an advertisement, or ad, is a public notice
a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out
I is the Roman numeral for one
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A notice-board opening is made by a devout person seeking a golden era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is a link joining the charade to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this Christian movement await the Second Coming and the thousand-year reign that follows.

clue.text: First words from pen aid scheme being hatched

indicators.note: a scheme being hatched is being cooked up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A plan to help prisoners is being devised.
explanation.definitionFit: A new parliamentarian's first address to the House is traditionally named this way.

clue.text: Horrified Arab leader met with stone — one knocked out

parts.note: an agha is a title for a chief or commander in the Middle East

indicators.note: the named word is removed from the other piece, as if knocked out of it

parts.note: the word stone is written in full here
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern chief is struck by a stone and someone is knocked out, to general horror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' removes ONE from STONE, leaving ST; 'met with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being filled with horror and shock means being appalled.

clue.text: Fictitious place — in short, not one in map book

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for map book

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps
the word not shortened, as in can't, is n't
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An imaginary place is not to be found in a map book.
explanation.walkthrough: NT + I go into ATLAS between ATLA and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The lost island described by Plato is a legendary land that never existed.

clue.text: A striker we found to be fantastic sportsman?

indicators.note: the letters are made fantastic, turned into something new

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: We discover that a striker is a brilliant sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone towed on skis behind a boat is a sportsman of a sort, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One may have spotted suits at work

definitions.text: One may have spotted suits at work

parts.words: One may have spotted suits at work
parts.note: spotted suits means stained clothes, not noticed people, so it is someone whose job is cleaning them

explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning business deals with stained garments brought in by customers, removing marks without water.

clue.text: Outdoor festival — cut a cheese

indicators.note: the word for festival is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a fete is an outdoor fair or festival

explanation.surface: Someone trims a cheese at a village fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last E of FETE, leaving FET; A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A white, crumbly Greek curd made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Desperate fellow drinking beers, male who may live in Yorkshire?

indicators.note: the fellow takes the other pieces inside him, as if drinking them

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the burly cowboy of the British comic The Dandy
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A desperate man drinking beer is a Yorkshire local.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a British comic-strip strongman. ALES and M go inside DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from the Yorkshire Dales, the valleys of northern England, is called this.

clue.text: Rescuer of limited number — gosh!

parts.note: No. is the shortened form of number
ah is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at how few were rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the ark saved only a limited number, which flavours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The patriarch who built the ark saved his family and the animals from the Flood.

clue.text: Like a great show with everyone under the sun? The opposite maybe

indicators.note: read with 'The opposite maybe', the first piece goes over, not under, the second

parts.note: all means everyone
the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A great show features everyone under the sun, or perhaps it is the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with everyone under the sun' suggests STAR then ALL; 'The opposite maybe' flips it so ALL sits above STAR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A production with a cast full of famous performers is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Article penned by performer at end of month as a dissenter

indicators.note: the performer comes after the month, at its end

parts.note: Sep is the short form of September

indicators.note: the article is enclosed by the performer, as if in a pen

parts.note: an artist is a performer
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article written by an artist at the end of the month is a dissenting piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks away from a larger body, wanting independence, dissents from it.

clue.text: Design home to have number, then fifty times as many

parts.note: in means at home
ten is a number
fifty times ten is five hundred, the Roman numeral D

explanation.surface: A domestic design gets a number, then fifty times that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' and 'then' are links; 'as many' refers back to TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To design something can mean to plan or mean it, as in having a purpose in mind.

clue.text: Spike is devilish type when given drink

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A drink spiked makes someone devilish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'when given' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something with a sharp point is to spike it.

clue.text: Controversial writer exposes European dimness

parts.note: a Pole is a European
mist causes dimness

explanation.surface: A polemical writer reveals the dim view held by a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person given to fierce written argument and dispute is a polemicist.

clue.text: Drink that's swallowed time and time again to make one stronger

indicators.note: the drink takes the other pieces inside, swallowing them

parts.note: beer is a drink
a second T for time

explanation.surface: A drink taken again and again to make someone strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovered from illness, one is healthier and fitter than before.

clue.text: What's done in river, a little depth below

indicators.note: in a down entry, the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales and England
d is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: Something happened in a river, with a little depth beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An act is a thing done, a feat or action.

clue.text: In part of the river US trainee gets into difficulties

indicators.note: the letters get into a mess and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: An American trainee gets into trouble in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the tidal mouth of a river.

clue.text: Religious person meddled — eyed doing a bunk

indicators.note: doing a bunk is British slang for running off, so the named word leaves

parts.note: monkeyed about means meddled

explanation.surface: A religious man interfered, was watched, then fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a bunk' (British slang for fleeing) removes EYED from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A man in a religious order living under vows is a holy brother.

clue.text: Hard bargaining that is part of stable business?

definitions.meaning: read literally, buying and selling equine animals kept in a stable

explanation.surface: Tough negotiation is part of running a stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for shrewd negotiation comes literally from dealing in animals that are ridden.
